text.title: Which Unattended Surface, If Any
text.summary: Routing from the trigger inventory and the exec requirement to a surface. Most systems terminate at the first branch, which installs nothing.

decision-tree.root-question: Listing every trigger: does any of them fire at a moment when no human is present?

conclusion.verdict: STOP. chosen_surface: none. Install nothing. The agent session you start yourself already runs this work, and its own hooks already fire on its own events. Record what you were about to install under rejected_surfaces and close the record.

STOP. chosen_surface: none until a real failure occurs. A surface adopted on anticipation ends up holding the tutorial workflow and an update schedule. Revisit the moment a run demonstrably does not happen.

Provision an always-on host and record its monthly cost in currency, or fall back to chosen_surface: none. A nightly job on a sleeping laptop does not fail — it is simply absent, which nothing reports.
chosen_surface: agent-hooks. Already installed, already monitored, nothing new to secure or update. Declare the blast radius and the stop switch and stop here.

chosen_surface: os-scheduler — cron, a systemd timer, the platform equivalent. Record why_hooks_insufficient as a missing capability, not a missing convenience, plus the blast radius and the stop switch.

Only a self-hosted n8n survives, with Execute Command explicitly re-enabled and the binary present inside the container that runs it. Make, Dify and Flowise cannot execute a local binary at all, and no cloud instance can. Re-verify against current docs before committing.
chosen_surface: workflow-runtime. Record both escalation justifications, keep it as the system's ONLY unattended surface, and put whatever it replaces in rejected_surfaces.
Overlay, refuse regardless of branch. Two surfaces either schedule a thing twice or each assume the other owns it; both failures surface late because the symptom is an absence. Replace, do not add.
